solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mum in the morning quietly rings cleaner

parts.note: 'mum' as in keep mum: a call for silence, written SH
AM, ante meridiem, before noon
P is piano, the musical direction for soft playing
two rings look like two letter Os

explanation.surface: A mother's early-morning routine: quietly ringing round for a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but is the command for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap, a product for washing hair or carpets.

clue.text: Secretly, Thai cult spread over island

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the concealed letters are read upwards, backwards
secretly means the letters lie concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A Thai cult has quietly spread across an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secretly' conceals AICULTS in the words; 'over' reads them backwards. 'spread' is part of the text, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: St Lucia is a Caribbean island nation in the Windward Islands.

clue.text: Misuse of salt is, in my opinion, very high

indicators.note: misuse of the following letters means they are put in a wrong order

parts.note: IMO is the texting abbreviation for in my opinion

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a salt is far too dear when misused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misuse of' turns SALT IS into ALTISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Altissimo is the musical term for the highest register of a voice or instrument.

clue.text: Broadcasting quiet section

indicators.note: broadcasting is putting out over the airwaves, so we hear a word

parts.note: peace is quiet, calm

explanation.surface: A quiet section of a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a part or portion of something larger.

clue.text: Love the Italian trifle, slicing part for Austin?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
il is Italian for the

indicators.note: slicing up the dessert's name breaks it into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loves an Italian trifle and slices off a portion for Austin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slicing' turns TRIFLE into FILTER. Austin is an old British car make, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil filter is an engine component, a spare part fitted to a car.

clue.text: Centre for enthusiasts addicted to revolutionary toy

parts.note: a mecca is any place that draws devotees of something

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the short word for addicted is read backwards

parts.note: to be 'on' a drug is to be addicted to it

explanation.surface: A toy so revolutionary that hobbyists flock to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like praise for the toy, but it turns the word for addicted round.
explanation.definitionFit: Meccano is a British construction kit of metal strips, nuts and bolts for children.

clue.text: Complaint upper-class politician put in document

indicators.note: put in means the pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for document

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a document
U denotes upper-class usage
MP, a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An upper-class politician files a complaint in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a viral illness, and a complaint is an ailment.

clue.text: Involve Tory, relative and aristocrat, briefly

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
sis is short for sister

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a toff is British slang for a posh person

explanation.surface: A Tory, a relative and a toff are briefly mixed up in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts TOFF to TOF.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made up of components is to comprise or involve them.

clue.text: In a state of harmony, make amends

definitions.meaning: to make reparation for a wrong

explanation.surface: Being at peace with oneself after putting things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words mean in accord; one word means to make reparation.

clue.text: Former pupil likes to edit column

parts.note: OB, old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: editing reworks the following word into a new letter order

explanation.surface: An old boy enjoys editing a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to edit' turns LIKES into ELISK. 'Column' is a pillar, not a newspaper feature.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar.

clue.text: Detest being without old woodworking machine

indicators.note: 'without' tells us the letter for old is dropped from the word for detest

parts.note: to detest is to loathe

explanation.surface: Someone hates working without their old woodworking machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins wood or metal against a cutting tool to shape it, a workshop machine.

clue.text: Charlie's word of approval for fish dish

parts.note: a charlie and a lemon are both British slang for a fool; the possessive gives the S
olé is the Spanish cry of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Charlie gives his verdict on a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is British slang for a fool, as is 'lemon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a flatfish commonly served as a restaurant course.

clue.text: This writer on Greek island reportedly marks beauty ware

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
the setter referring to himself, ME

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear a word that sounds like the synonym for marks

parts.note: ticks are check marks

explanation.surface: A writer holidaying on a Greek island notes down beauty products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes TICKS sound like TICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetics are make-up and similar products, things sold to enhance appearance.

clue.text: Reserve recalled in ancient race

parts.note: ice is coldness of manner, as is reserve

indicators.note: recalled, called back, means the small word is reversed

explanation.surface: A reserve is recalled to fight in an ancient race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests troops, but it means coolness of manner; 'recalled' reverses the little word 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe, led by Boudicca, so a people or race.

clue.text: Devout sect wrongly tailed husband

indicators.note: tailed means docked, its last letter cut

parts.note: amiss means wrongly, as in 'taken amiss'

explanation.surface: A devout sect wrongly followed a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailed' cuts the last S from AMISS to give AMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amish are a strict Christian group in the USA living without modern technology.

clue.text: Controversial issue animated King Edward perhaps

parts.note: hot means heated, animated
King Edward is a popular British variety of potato

explanation.surface: A lively King Edward becomes a topic of debate.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch but is a potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter too awkward to handle, a delicate subject everyone wants rid of.

clue.text: Rolled oats course that's on the breakfast table?

indicators.note: rolled oats are flattened, and here the word oats is rolled about into a new order

parts.note: a racecourse is a track

explanation.surface: Rolled oats are a breakfast course on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolled' gives TOAS from OATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast rack is the slotted holder that keeps slices upright at breakfast.

clue.text: Academy individual's occupied rebuilding the rack, a type of punishment

indicators.note: occupied means the single letter sits inside the other piece
rebuilding signals the letters of the phrase are rearranged

parts.note: I is one, an individual; the 's stands for 'has'

explanation.surface: A school rebuilds its rack, an old form of punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding' turns THE RACK into THCKEAR; 'occupied' puts I in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip round the ear, a swollen ear from a blow, given as chastisement.

clue.text: Throw nuts into spacious environment for such birds?

indicators.note: the surrounding word forms an environment for the other piece

parts.note: airy means open, spacious

indicators.note: nuts, crazy, signals the letters of throw are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone throws nuts into a roomy space for birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' turns THROW into WORTH. The birds are aircraft, so fit to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes, nicknamed birds, are certified fit to fly.

clue.text: American paint remover's a disappointment to worker's latest companion

parts.note: a blow is a setback or disappointment

indicators.note: latest picks the final letter of worker's

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A worker's new companion finds the paint remover a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remover's' stands for 'remover is'. BLOWTORCH is the American term for the British blowlamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A flame torch strips paint by softening it; the American name for this tool.

clue.text: Crow around centre of Mumbai finding hot air

indicators.note: around means the brag word encloses the other piece

parts.note: to crow is to brag or boast

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letters of Mumbai

explanation.surface: A crow circling central Mumbai finds hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' is a verb, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, empty talk, figuratively hot air.

clue.text: Loudly supporting peripheral characters in theatre

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: the outermost letters of the next word are taken

explanation.surface: Supporting actors on the edges of a theatre speak up loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripheral characters in' takes T and E from theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Forte is the musical direction meaning play strongly, with great volume.

clue.text: Apply gold to enrich run-down fence

indicators.note: to enrich is to add precious content inside
a run-down fence is broken, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gilding a dilapidated fence to make it more valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run-down' gives ENFCE from the fence; 'to enrich' means the heraldic gold goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply a rule or law is to impose it.

clue.text: Graduate with plum job, regularly missing European city

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: every other letter is left out, so alternate letters of the phrase remain

explanation.surface: A graduate keeps missing out on a plum job in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly missing' drops P, U, J, B and leaves LMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmo (Malmö) is a port city in southern Sweden.

clue.text: Foreign transporter rejected precinct area

indicators.note: rejected, sent back, means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a shopping precinct is a mall

explanation.surface: A foreign carrier turned away from a shopping zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MALLA round.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American pack animal, a beast of burden abroad.

clue.text: List of completed jobs might be thus torn into

definitions.text: List of completed jobs might be thus
definitions.meaning: items on a to-do list are checked once done
scolded or reprimanded, being told off

explanation.surface: A list of finished jobs gets ripped up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both checked as done and reprimanded.

clue.text: Shabby, like equestrian gear?

definitions.meaning: tack is saddles and bridles for horses, so this means resembling tack

explanation.surface: A shabby look like worn riding kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacky means tawdry; whimsically, it also means having to do with tack.

clue.text: Tea left out, which might be on the house

definitions.text: which might be on the house

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: tea leaves, the dried leaves for brewing

explanation.surface: Tea left out at a café, offered free on the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the house' means free of charge on the surface, but literally the roof edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The overhanging lower edges of a roof form part of a building.

clue.text: Agonise when describing terrible naval deluge

indicators.note: describing is drawing round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to ache is to suffer pain, to agonise

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of naval are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a terrible naval disaster at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles the naval letters to VALAN; 'describing' means the word for agonise draws round them.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is an overwhelming flood of something, figuratively a deluge.

clue.text: One elects to put in minister from the right

indicators.note: reading from the right means the result is turned backwards
put in means one short word goes inside the abbreviation for the clergyman

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: Someone chooses to install a minister of the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the right' reads like politics but means reading backwards, giving RETOV reversed once 'put in' has placed the short word inside the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone casting a ballot in an election chooses representatives.

clue.text: Jasmine's warmed by such coast swimming around end of the year

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the single letter
swimming, moving about, signals coast is rearranged
end of picks the final letter of the

explanation.surface: Jasmine warms up on the coast after a swim at the year's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns COAST into TACOS, which goes 'around' E, the end of 'the', giving TEACOS; Y follows. Jasmine here is jasmine tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cosy is a padded cover keeping a teapot hot.

clue.text: Change locks on animal enclosure (extremely loose)

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a business letter
a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: extremely picks the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Change the locks on a pig pen, as they are loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' are hair, not door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: To restyle hair is to give the tresses a new cut or arrangement.
